text: Following is the process of Container Inspection and Repair (CIR) operation for a Container Industry Company: The CIR is performed in a yard spread over 13 acres and has 50 inspection points. Once a container arrives at the entry gate of the yard, the staff involved verifies the transporter’s documents based on the company guidelines. Once the documents are verified, they are entered into the Container Information System (CIS). This gate is manned 24x7x365 as the data from this system is vital to the further processing in the CIR operation. The next stage is surveying and inspection process followed by an estimation of damages. This activity is outsourced to a specialist company which surveys, inspects and prepares an estimation report. Damages up to Rs 1000 are approved automatically and can be directly transferred to the awaiting repair stack. Beyond this limit, a system entry is prepared and the approval from a higher authority is needed to proceed further. Heavily damaged containers are removed directly from the facility and are not accepted until the damages are cleared. If the repair slots are free and the approvals are received, then the repair operation can begin. The yard contains 50 Pre- Trip Inspections (PTI) points. The PTI is carried out in order to determine whether the machinery units aye in working condition or not. It is imperative that any defects be detected in this process in order to prevent machine failure during use. \ ¥ Some’ A the inefficiencies in the system are as follows: Delays in data entry at the gate contribute significantly to delays in the estimation process. The company has other yards where this operation is being performed and data from the other yards are communicated to the company via email. Currently the inspection process is manual and hence lacks automation. After surveying also, the containers are stacked manually which is time consuming and individual containers cannot be tracked. Vb Qla) Develop a Business Process Model Diagram to map the existing process. Qlb) Using the DMAIC Approach suggest means to improve the existing process by clearly articulating the process measurement yardsticks.

question_stem: Following is the process of Vendor Payment Reimbursement Process in a leading Consumer Bank in India:
text: consumer bank has several sales and marketing payments to be made to various vendors associated with their various Products (Consumer loans). These vendors would conduct various promotional activities for the bank which included advertising in newspapers, loan melas, free gifts, gold coins, etc. to attract more loan sales. In order to incentivize the vendors, the bank reimbursed a specific percentage of the expenses incurred by the vendors. There were however, strict guidelines with regard the nature of activities which are eligible for a reimbursement. Some of these included — Prior permission to conduct an event, bill processing within a fixed time, a maximum limit on the budget which must be pre approved by the sales heads ete failing which the bill would not be processed and hence not refunded. Every event is first checked from the feasibility point of view and either the vendor approaches the bank with the proposal or the bank’s relationship manager (RM) instructs the vendor about the event. The proposal is sent to a senior RM for approval based on the guidelines for approval } and budget available to the branch. If an approval is received by the vendor, the activity is aT and the vendor sends the bills within a week after the completion of the event to the bank. The backend sales team receives the bills and checks the bills and supported documentation. These are checked with respect to a checklist specified by the bank. It is the responsibility of the RM to check the details of the bills as well. Once the details are found to be correct, the backend sales tearn updates the bills in the system and a senior manager approves them. Once the bills are approved, a payment request memo (PRM) is prepared based on a pre-defined template and attached along the bills and supporting documents and sent to the Product team. Vo Once the Product Manager, approves the bills, the accounts department issues the cheques as per the bill amount. The cheques are collected by the Product team within 2-3 days and the details of the cheque are entered in the system or maintained in excel. The product team then sends the cheque to the sales team which then gives it to the respective vendor(s) Some of the problems faced by the departments are as follows — The relationship manager and sales manager tend to approve promotional events which end up exceeding their budgets. There is no information on the number of promotional events approved events conducted and number of bills received. There are always a set of pending bills which are either not received or not entered in the system. In case there is a bill which exceeds the budget, it cannot be entered in the system until additional budget is allocated leading to delay in processing the payments. Some RMs are not checking the bills as per the checklist and some do not even know about the existence of a checklist. Bills are often not approved using the system and are approved by email making the information in the system inconsistent with the actual status of the bills. A copy of the bills is not maintained at the Sales office and hence it becomes difficult to clarify at a later point of time in case of any discrepancies. As a result of all the above mentioned problems, the sales team is not in a position to commit to the vendor when their payments will be ready. Qla) Develop a Business Process Model Diagram to map the existing process. Qib) Using the DMAIC Approach suggest means to improve the existing process by clearly articulating the process measurement yardsticks.
